source.heading: PASSAGE II
source.directions: The passage below has gaps. Immediately following each gap, four options are provided. Choose the most appropriate option for each gap.
source.attribution: Adapted from Timo, A. (1987) A Guide to the Study of O' Level English Language, Ibadan: UPL

passage.text: Mr. Ikimi, the headmaster, decided to erect a new science block.
He awarded the {{6}} to a well-known {{7}} who drew up a {{8}} which was sent to the Town Planning Authority for approval.
The {{9}} which had been chosen was cleared and {{10}} engaged to start work on laying the foundation of which the most important process was pouring the {{11}}.
Very soon the building took {{12}} and the roof was on in no time.

The {{13}} done by a set of very competent carpenters, was intricately interwoven, and louver windows added extra beauty to the new block, whose exterior walls looked most striking after the second {{14}} had been put on.
The interior {{15}} was left to the competent domestic science teacher.

questions.stem: He awarded the ...6... to a well-known ...

options.why: In building projects, you award a contract for the execution of the work.
You carry out a project, but the formal agreement awarded is a contract.
An assignment is a task given to a student or employee, not awarded for construction.
You do not award a business to a professional to put up a building.

questions.stem: ... to a well-known ...7... who drew up a ...

options.why: An architect is the professional who designs buildings and draws up plans for Town Planning approval.
Designer is too general; building plans for planning approval are drawn by an architect.
Engineers handle structural calculations or construction work, whereas the architect draws up the building plan.
Town planners approve plans at the Authority; the architect draws them up.

questions.clue: drew up a … for the Town Planning Authority

questions.stem: ... who drew up a ...8... which was sent to the Town Planning Authority for approval.

options.why: An architect draws up a building plan and submits it to the Town Planning Authority.
Planning authorities approve technical building plans, not ordinary pictures.
A chart displays data or maps, not an architectural building design.
A programme is a schedule of events, not a drawing sent for building approval.

questions.clue: drew up a … sent to the Town Planning Authority

questions.stem: The ...9... which had been chosen was cleared ...

options.why: Spot is informal and too small for a building plot.
Locality means the wider neighbourhood, not the specific piece of land cleared for a building.
In construction, the piece of ground chosen and cleared for building is called the site.
Environment refers to surrounding conditions, not a plot of land to be cleared.

questions.stem: ... and ...10... engaged to start work on laying the foundation ...

options.why: Worker is too general; laying foundations with concrete is the job of a mason.
A mason is a skilled builder who lays foundations, bricks, stones and concrete.
An artist does not lay building foundations.
A plumber fits water pipes, not building foundations.

questions.clue: engaged to start work on laying the foundation

questions.stem: ... of which the most important process was pouring the ...11....

options.why: Marble is cut into slabs for floors or walls; it is not poured for foundations.
Concrete (cement, sand, gravel and water) is mixed and poured to form a building foundation.
Laterite is reddish soil used for filling or roads, not poured into a foundation.
Loose sand alone is not poured to set a foundation.

questions.stem: Very soon the building took ...12... and the roof was on in no time.

options.why: Take position means to stand in a place, not to develop into a recognisable structure.
To take shape is the fixed idiom meaning to develop into a clear or finished form.
Take place means to happen (used for events), not for a building rising.
Take direction is not used to describe a building rising.

questions.stem: The ...13... done by a set of very competent carpenters, was intricately interwoven ...

options.why: Carpenters work with wood, so the timber framing, doors and roof trusses they make are called woodwork.
Wood fixing is not the standard building term for carpentry work.
Wood cutting is only sawing timber, whereas carpenters build and fit the wooden structures.
Woodwork is the standard single noun for what carpenters make in a building.

questions.clue: done by a set of very competent carpenters

questions.stem: ... whose exterior walls looked most striking after the second ...14... had been put on.

options.why: Spraying names an application method, not a layer of paint put on walls.
You do not put on a second washing to make exterior walls look striking.
A coating is a layer of paint or plaster applied to exterior walls.
Covering is too vague; paint on walls is applied in coats or coatings.

questions.clue: exterior walls looked most striking after the second

questions.stem: The interior ...15... was left to the competent domestic science teacher.

options.why: A domestic science teacher finishes the inside look after building is complete, which is interior decoration rather than structural design.
Interior dressing is not the standard English collocation.
Planning takes place before construction, not after the walls are painted.
Interior decoration is the standard collocation for furnishing and beautifying the inside of a finished room.

questions.clue: The interior … left to the competent domestic science teacher
